title: The counter that wrapped
hook: Add one to a very large number. The answer depends on where you are.
concept: Each language decides how many bits a number has and what happens at the edge. Java int wraps around to a negative number. JavaScript numbers never wrap at 32 bits but stop counting exactly above 2^53. Python integers simply keep growing.

worlds.js: The first line is fine because numbers are doubles. The second silently returns 9007199254740992, the same number you started with. Large ids from a database can be corrupted this way.
worlds.python: Integers have no fixed size, so both lines are correct. Nothing to fix in this world.
worlds.java: int wraps to -2147483648 without any error. long holds 64 bits, so the second line is correct.

fix: Pick a type that is wide enough for the value (long in Java, BigInt or strings for ids in JavaScript), and validate ranges where numbers enter your system.
